dedupe_keys.name: global e waste monitor and national e waste statistics itu and unitar global e waste statistics partnership

description: The Global E-waste Monitor is the main international source of statistics on electronic waste, published since 2014 and in its 2024 edition by the Global E-waste Statistics Partnership of the International Telecommunication Union and the UN Institute for Training and Research. It reports e-waste generated, documented formal collection and recycling, and policies by country and region: from 2010 to 2022 e-waste generated rose from 34 to 62 billion kg while documented recycling rose from 8 to 13.8 billion kg, and in June 2023 81 countries had e-waste policy, legislation or regulation. The site also hosts regional and national monitors, from the Western Balkans and West Asia to Kenya, Norway and Tajikistan, a Global Transboundary E-waste Flows monitor, and the third edition of the e-waste statistics guidelines on classifications and indicators. Reports are free PDF downloads with country statistics. Caveats: figures for many countries are modelled from sales and lifespan estimates, not measured, informal recycling is poorly documented, and editions revise earlier numbers. Simulation uses: estimating e-waste flows and recycling capacity needs, building transboundary waste trade networks, and linking electronics consumption to waste infrastructure planning. Related records: Basel Convention national reporting (data-basel-convention-national-reporting) and Eurostat waste shipments (data-eurostat-env-wasship-transboundary-waste-shipments) cover transboundary movements.
